title: Superstitious personality infected Thriving Isle color choice (picked Red in mono-blue deck)
description:
In game_20260302_174929_g4, Grok4F Lucky (grok-4-fast, superstitious personality) chose Red for Thriving Isle's color selection despite playing a mono-blue deck with zero red cards. The chat message sent in the same LLM response says 'Thriving Isle taps in red-hot for that extra spice -- shuffle's got that lucky red glow today!' — strong evidence that the superstitious personality drove the color choice rather than strategic analysis.

Impact: Zero in this game (the ability was never activated and the opponent was dead the same turn). But in a longer game, permanently wasting Thriving Isle's second color on an unusable color is a real strategic cost.

This is a personality infection case: the chat personality (superstitious / lucky) bled into an actual gameplay decision. The model has hidden reasoning (grok-4-fast doesn't expose reasoning tokens via OpenRouter) so we can't confirm the internal reasoning, but the circumstantial evidence from the chat message is strong.

Note: The superstitious personality was otherwise clean — 15 chat messages were sent, all heavily themed around luck/karma/hot streaks, but all other gameplay decisions were sound (lands on curve, correct aura sequencing, efficient attacks).

Evidence:
- ~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260302_174929_g4/Grok4F Lucky_llm.jsonl seq=171 (color choice), seq=174 (chat message)
- Game export annotations confirm good play otherwise
